regions.text: 間に夕食をすまさう』（第三葉第六場）。

quote.translation: Now, we shall finish supper in the morning" (Act III, Scene 6).

regions.text: 肉織の解剖と酷薄な心の取調、裸體と服制、朝の間と夕食。親念の措定に充足な理由が続けてゐる。

quote.translation: The anatomy of a body and the examination of a cruel heart, nakedness and dress, the morning and supper: the positing of ideas here lacks a sufficient ground.

regions.text: ゐる。藝術が一方に於て夢と狂無とに接近しながら他方に於て達別を有つこと

quote.translation: It is often said that art, whilst it approaches dream and madness on the one hand, differs from them on the other.

regions.text: 藝術が一方に於て夢と狂無とに接近しながら他方に於て達別を有つことは度々説かれるところであるが、或種の藝術制作には理由約滑極約偶然が極度に現はれてるて、夢または狂氣そのものを思はしめるものがある。

quote.translation: In certain kinds of artistic production, however, negative contingency of ground appears to an extreme degree, and some works make us think of dream or madness itself.

regions.text: 例へば萬葉集第十六に心の考く所無き歌が二首ある。「吾妹子が響に生ひたる姫の戦れの秘の上の縮」「吾背子が徹祭にする眼形の吉野の山にが織ぞさがれる』。

quote.translation: Book Sixteen of the Man'yōshū, for example, contains two "poems to which the mind attaches nothing": "On my beloved's brow there grows / the sugoroku bull's / saddle, the sore upon it", and "The round stone my husband makes his loincloth: / on the mountains of Yoshino / icefish hang".

regions.text: 食人親王が「もし由る所無き歌を作る人あらば、賜ふに錢帛を以てせむ』といふ合を簽せられた結果として出來た歌である。「由るところ無き」とは理由の非存在の謂に他ならない。

quote.translation: These poems were made in response to an order issued by Prince Toneri, "If there is anyone who makes a poem with nothing it rests on, I will reward him with coin and silk", and "with nothing it rests on" means nothing other than the non-existence of a ground.

regions.text: 歌経標式の「離會」の歌「春日山降酒ぐ船の薬師寺淡路の島のの形」も同機である。営葉と言葉との間に何箏の論理的聯絡がない。

quote.translation: The "rikai" poem of the Kakyō hyōshiki, "Kasuga mountain, a boat rowing over the peak, Yakushiji, the island of Awaji, the mouldboard of a plough", is of the same kind.

regions.text: 積極のものは殆を見出すことは出來ないで、語脈にあつて理由の非存在が消極的に目撃されてゐるに止まるものである。

quote.translation: Between one word and the next there is no logical connection at all, so that almost nothing positive can be found in it, and in the run of the words the non-existence of a ground is only witnessed negatively.

regions.text: しかしなほそこに何等かの機術があることを拒むことは出來ない。

quote.translation: Yet we still cannot deny that there is some art in it.

regions.text: シュークスビャの「真夏の夜の変は偶然の抽象

quote.translation: Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream is an example of the symbolisation of the abstract nonsense of chance, and at the same time a realistic depiction of the most concrete truth of human life.
